triples.relationship: opposition between corrupt preferences and the call to good
triples.rationale: Micah accuses leaders of hating good and seeking evil. Amos calls for seeking good rather than evil and restoring judgment, directly opposing the preferences Micah condemns.
triples.source_text: you who hate good things and seek evil things, who snatch their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?”

target_units.text: Seek the good and not the evil, so that you may live; then the Lord God Almighty will be with you, just as you said,
“We have hated evil things and loved good things.” Restore judgment at the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on Joseph’s remaining ones.

triples.relationship: shared imagery of devouring the people
triples.rationale: Micah describes the people's flesh treated as meat for a cooking pot. The psalm similarly accuses lawless people of devouring the people like a meal of bread. Both use eating imagery to portray abuse of the people.
triples.source_text: Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,

target_units.text: Will all those who practice lawlessness not know? Those who devour my people as a meal of bread did not call upon the Lord.

triples.relationship: violence followed by rejected prayer
triples.rationale: Micah says the Lord will not hear the cry of those who acted wickedly against the people and will turn His face away. Isaiah likewise says He will turn His eyes away and refuse multiplied supplications because their hands are full of blood.
triples.source_text: so they will cry to the Lord, but He will not listen to them. He will turn His face away from them at that time, because they acted wickedly in their practices against them.

target_units.text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.

triples.relationship: corrupt prophetic pronouncements tied to food
triples.rationale: Micah's misleading prophets proclaim peace when their mouths are supplied and raise war when they are not. Ezekiel condemns profaning God through vain pronouncements for barley and scraps of bread; both connect deceptive prophetic activity with food received.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace to him; but when nothing was put into their mouths, they raised war against him:

target_units.text: They were profaning Me among My people for a handful of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death lives that ought not die and preserving lives that ought not live, as you uttered things to a people listening to vain pronouncements.

triples.relationship: shared judgment imagery of lost daylight
triples.rationale: Micah announces night in place of vision and sunset over the prophets. Amos similarly announces the sun setting at midday and light becoming dark during daytime. Micah applies the darkness specifically to the prophets' loss of vision.
triples.source_text: “Therefore you will have night instead of vision and darkness instead of divination; the sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will darken over them.

target_units.text: “On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

triples.relationship: prophets ashamed of their visions
triples.rationale: Micah announces shame for dream-seers and mockery for diviners. Zechariah likewise says prophets will be ashamed because of their visions when they prophesy.
triples.source_text: Those seeing dreams will be ashamed and the diviners mocked; all of them will speak against them, because there will be no one listening to them,

target_units.text: On that day the prophets will be ashamed, each because of his vision when he prophesies; they will wear a hairy skin because they lied.

triples.relationship: commission to declare Jacob's sins
triples.rationale: Micah links strength in the Lord's Spirit with declaring Jacob's impieties and Israel's sins. Isaiah likewise commands a strong public proclamation of the people's sins and Jacob's lawless acts.
triples.source_text: unless I fill up strength in the Spirit of the Lord and of judgment and might, to declare to Jacob his impieties and to Israel his sins.”

target_units.text: “Shout with strength and do not spare! Raise your voice like a trumpet and announce My people’s sins to them, and Jacob’s house their lawless acts.

triples.relationship: perverted justice opposed to the legal requirement
triples.rationale: Micah charges leaders with abhorring justice and twisting what is straight. Deuteronomy forbids perverting judgment and commands pursuit of what is just, directly opposing that conduct.
triples.source_text: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,

target_units.text: They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.
You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.

triples.relationship: parallel condemnation of building with bloodshed
triples.rationale: Micah condemns building Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices. Habakkuk pronounces woe on building and preparing a city with bloodshed and injustices, repeating the distinctive city-building accusation.
triples.source_text: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!

target_units.text: Woe to the one building a city with bloodshed and preparing a city with injustices!

triples.relationship: judicial payment opposed to the ban on bribes
triples.rationale: Micah accuses Jerusalem's leaders of judging for gifts. Deuteronomy explicitly forbids judges taking a bribe because it blinds the wise and overturns righteous words.
triples.source_text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”

target_units.text: They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.

triples.relationship: explicit later citation of Micah's warning
triples.rationale: Jeremiah explicitly attributes to Micah the warning that Zion will be plowed as a field and the house's mountain become woodland. Those clauses correspond to this verse; Jeremiah's description of Jerusalem as an untrodden place is preserved alongside Micah's fruit watcher's hut wording.
triples.source_text: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.

target_units.text: Micah the Morathite lived in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah’s people: Thus said the Lord: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become an untrodden place, and the house’s mountain a grove of woodland.

Did Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the Lord’s face, and the Lord ceased from the evils He spoke against them? And we have done great evils against our own lives!

triples.relationship: parallel oracle of the elevated Lord's mountain
triples.rationale: Both passages locate the vision in the last days, raise the Lord's mountain above surrounding heights and describe peoples or nations coming toward it.
triples.source_text: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, established upon the mountain summits and raised above the hills, and peoples will hurry toward it.

target_units.text: In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

triples.relationship: parallel invitation to learn at Zion
triples.rationale: Both passages have nations invite one another to the Lord's mountain and Jacob's God's house, to learn His way and walk in it. Both end with law going from Zion and the Lord's word from Jerusalem.
triples.source_text: Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. They will show us His way, and we will walk in His paths.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

target_units.text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: parallel transformation of weapons into tools
triples.rationale: Both describe divine judgment among peoples followed by swords becoming plows and spears becoming sickles. Each concludes with nations no longer taking up war or learning to wage it.
triples.source_text: He will judge between many peoples and reprove strong nations as far as a distant land. They will cut their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will certainly no longer raise sword against nation, nor will they learn to wage war anymore.

target_units.text: He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.

triples.relationship: contrasting prophetic uses of weapons and farming tools
triples.rationale: Micah describes weapons remade into farming tools as war ends. Joel reverses that direction, ordering farming tools made into weapons while gathering nations for judgment. The same implements serve contrasting scenes in their respective oracles.
triples.source_text: He will judge between many peoples and reprove strong nations as far as a distant land. They will cut their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will certainly no longer raise sword against nation, nor will they learn to wage war anymore.

target_units.text: Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into lances; let the powerless say, “I am strong!”
Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.

triples.relationship: parallel vine-and-fig-tree peace imagery
triples.rationale: Micah promises rest beneath each person's vine and fig tree without fear. Zechariah likewise pictures neighbors invited beneath a vine and fig tree in the promised day.
triples.source_text: Each will rest beneath his vine and each beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one causing fear, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.

target_units.text: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each of you will invite his neighbor beneath a vine and beneath a fig tree.”

triples.relationship: shared declaration of allegiance to the Lord
triples.rationale: Micah contrasts the peoples' own ways with the community's lasting walk in the Lord's name. Joshua similarly contrasts available objects of service with his household's declared service of the Lord.
triples.source_text: For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.

target_units.text: But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”

triples.relationship: parallel gathering of the crushed and rejected
triples.rationale: Micah promises to gather the crushed and receive the expelled. Zephaniah likewise promises gathering of the crushed and saving and receiving the oppressed and rejected.
triples.source_text: “On that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather the crushed one, receive the expelled one and those I rejected.

target_units.text: I will gather the crushed. Alas! Who took up reproach against her?
Look, I am acting within you for your sake at that time, says the Lord. I will save the oppressed and the rejected; I will receive them and make them a boast and renowned throughout the earth.

triples.relationship: the Lord's kingship associated with Mount Zion
triples.rationale: Micah promises that the Lord will reign over the restored people on Mount Zion. Obadiah likewise joins people ascending from Mount Zion with the declaration that the kingdom will be the Lord's.
triples.source_text: I will make the crushed one a remnant and the rejected one a strong nation. The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever.

target_units.text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

triples.relationship: Zion's distress compared to labor pains
triples.rationale: Micah asks why Zion has been seized with pains like a woman giving birth. Jeremiah likewise describes the daughter of Zion's voice and groaning as those of a woman in labor amid calamity.
triples.source_text: And now why have you experienced calamities? Did you have no king? Has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?

target_units.text: For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!

triples.relationship: rescue from Babylon
triples.rationale: Micah announces that Zion will reach Babylon and that the Lord will redeem her there from enemies. Isaiah calls the people to leave Babylon and proclaim that the Lord rescued His servant Jacob.
triples.source_text: Labor in birth, be courageous and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth! For now you will go out from the city, camp in the plain and come as far as Babylon. From there He will rescue you, and from there the Lord your God will redeem you from your enemies’ hand.

target_units.text: Leave Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Announce a voice of rejoicing, and let this be heard; proclaim it to the earth’s extremity. Say, “The Lord rescued His slave Jacob.”

triples.relationship: hostile rejoicing over Judah's distress
triples.rationale: Micah describes gathered nations declaring that they will rejoice over Zion. Obadiah explicitly forbids rejoicing and boasting over Judah's destruction and affliction, condemning the response Micah attributes to the hostile nations.
triples.source_text: Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”

target_units.text: Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

triples.relationship: gathered nations compared to an agricultural judgment
triples.rationale: Micah says the nations have been gathered like sheaves on a threshing floor despite not understanding God's counsel. Joel likewise gathers nations for judgment and depicts a ready vintage and full winepress. The agricultural forms differ, but both portray their gathering as preparation for judgment.
triples.source_text: But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.

target_units.text: Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.

triples.relationship: Israel equipped for threshing imagery of victory
triples.rationale: Micah equips Zion with iron horns and bronze hooves to thresh and grind peoples. Isaiah makes Jacob like saw-toothed threshing wagon wheels that grind mountains and hills into dust. Both portray the people as divinely equipped threshing instruments.
triples.source_text: Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. With them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine; you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.

target_units.text: Jacob, little Israel. I helped you,’ says God who redeems you, Israel.
Behold, I made you like new, saw-toothed wagon wheels for threshing. You will thresh mountains, grind hills fine, and make them like dust.
You will winnow, and wind will take them and a storm scatter them. But you will rejoice among Israel’s holy ones. And they will exult—

triples.relationship: shared image of humiliating blows to the cheeks
triples.rationale: Micah announces that Israel's tribes will be struck on the cheek with a rod. Isaiah's speaker gives his cheeks to slaps and faces shameful spitting. The connection is the depicted facial humiliation; the passages' subjects are preserved as distinct.
triples.source_text: Now the daughter of Ephraim will be fenced in with a barrier; he has set a constraint upon us. With a rod they will strike Israel’s tribes on the cheek.

target_units.text: I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.

triples.relationship: explicit later use of the Bethlehem ruler oracle
triples.rationale: Micah announces a ruler for Israel coming from Bethlehem. Matthew explicitly introduces a prophetic text naming Bethlehem as the ruler's birthplace in response to the question about the Christ. Matthew's by-no-means-least formulation remains distinct from Micah's smallness wording.
triples.source_text: And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are small to be among Judah’s thousands; from you one will come out for Me to be a ruler in Israel, and his goings out are from the beginning, from days of old.

target_units.text: He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what has been written through the prophet:
‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel.’”
